native_mcp_support.notes: The hosted DeepSeek API does not speak the MCP protocol natively. It offers OpenAI-compatible function calling (and an Anthropic-compatible API endpoint). MCP can be enabled at the serving-stack layer (e.g., SGLang MCP adapter) when self-hosting.

skills_concept.notes: DeepSeek has no first-party 'skills' or assistant-extension mechanism. The closest analog is the disk-based context caching (KV cache) which reduces the cost of repeated static prefixes such as tool definitions and system prompts. No persistent memory or packaged skill bundles exist.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Exact training cutoff not publicly documented in the technical report or model card as of 2026-06-21. Benchmarks suggest knowledge extends into early 2026.

context_window_tokens.notes: config.json: max_position_embeddings=1048576 (1M). Native config uses YaRN RoPE scaling with original_max_position_embeddings=65536 and factor=16.

input_output_shared.notes: Standard shared context pool: context_length=1M, max_output=384K. Input + output together consume the window.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived as context_window (1048576) minus max_output (384K = 393216) = 655360. Exact max_input not separately documented; operator-configurable when self-hosting.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Default output cap not separately documented in the API; only a maximum of 384K is stated. Deployment default may be lower; unconfirmed.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: 384K tokens maximum output across both thinking and non-thinking modes per the official pricing/model details page (384*1024=393216). For Think Max mode, model card recommends setting context window to at least 384K.

extended_context.notes: 1M is the standard GA context; no separate beta/extended window documented.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking/CoT tokens (reasoning_content) are billed as output tokens at the same output rate ($0.87/1M for V4-Pro). The 384K max_output cap covers both thinking and final response tokens combined.

tokenizer_family.notes: config.json: vocab_size=129280. Uses a custom encoding pipeline (encoding_dsv4) rather than a standard Jinja chat template. Same tokenizer family as V3/V3.2 (vocab_size 129280 shared across all DeepSeek V3/V4 generations).

tokenizer_access.value: HF AutoTokenizer (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro) + encoding_dsv4 Python scripts in repo
tokenizer_access.notes: Official tokenizer zip also available at https://cdn.deepseek.com/api-docs/deepseek_v3_tokenizer.zip per token usage docs.

image_token_rule.notes: V4-Pro is text-only; no image modality documented.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Official docs state ~1 English character ≈ 0.3 tokens (= ~3.3 chars/token). Use as rough estimate only; actual ratio varies by content.

function_calling.notes: Full OpenAI-compatible function calling with parallel tool calls, strict mode (beta), and tool use in both thinking and non-thinking modes.

native_mcp.notes: The hosted API does not accept raw MCP messages. When self-hosting with SGLang, an MCP adapter can be layered on.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: API returns multiple tool_calls in a single response turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: No documented hard limit on number of tools per request. Effective limit is the context window (tool defs count as input tokens).

max_tools_practical.notes: No DeepSeek-specific empirical degradation data found. Estimate based on general community consensus (~30-50 tools) from Berkeley FCL research. Treat as low-confidence.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI-compatible format: {type: 'function', function: {name, description, parameters}} with optional strict mode. Also accepts Anthropic-format tools via the /anthropic endpoint.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are part of the prompt and billed as input tokens. They are eligible for disk KV-cache hits.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No progressive/deferred tool loading in the DeepSeek API. All tools must be in the request.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Strict mode (beta) supports a defined subset of JSON Schema types: object, string, number, integer, boolean, array, enum, anyOf, $ref/$def. minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems not supported in strict mode.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap; description counts against context window.

max_request_size.notes: No vendor byte cap; bounded by serving config (vLLM --max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Context-bound; tool results count against max_model_len.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Depends on the model chat-template tool-call parser; see parallel_tool_calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: Set by the agent host/framework, not the model.

max_total_tools.notes: No vendor cap. Effective ceiling ≈ (context_window − output headroom) ÷ avg tool-definition tokens, set by serving config. Client hosts may cap lower (Cursor ~40, Claude Desktop ~100).

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Open-weight: the model API layer imposes NO tool count/size caps. Binding limits come from (1) the serving stack — vLLM/SGLang max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens, GPU KV-cache; (2) the model chat-template tool-call parser (must match --tool-call-parser); (3) the agent host (Cursor ~40-tool cap, Claude Desktop ~100). vLLM's default context is often 16K which silently truncates tool calls — raise --max-model-len.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: No skills/extension mechanism. No persistent memory or packaged capability bundles.

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System prompts count as input tokens and are eligible for disk KV-cache. In multi-turn agentic workflows (e.g., Claude Code integration), reasoning_content from tool-call turns must be passed back and is billed as input.

prompt_caching.notes: Disk-based KV-cache (context caching) enabled by default for all users. Cache hits for V4-Pro: $0.003625/1M vs $0.435/1M cache-miss (>99% discount). Cache persists for hours to days and matches common prefixes automatically. Tool definitions and system prompts are prime caching candidates.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent memory feature in the API.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache-miss (standard) input price. Self-hosting: cost is compute only (no per-token fee).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Thinking/CoT tokens billed at this same output rate.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache hit (disk KV-cache) price for V4-Pro. >99% discount vs cache-miss.

batch_discount.notes: No batch API discount documented as of 2026-06-21.

billing_unit.notes: Hosted API bills per token. Self-hosted: compute cost only.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: reasoning_content (CoT/thinking) tokens count as output tokens and are billed at $0.87/1M. The 384K max_output cap includes thinking tokens.

weights_url.notes: Also available at ModelScope: https://modelscope.cn/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Base model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base.

param_variants.value: 1.6T total / 49B active (MoE). FP4+FP8 mixed precision instruct weights; FP8 base weights.
param_variants.notes: MoE: 384 routed experts, 6 active per token, 1 shared expert. 61 hidden layers.

native_context_config.notes: config.json max_position_embeddings=1048576 via YaRN RoPE scaling (factor=16, original=65536).

serving_frameworks.value: vLLM, SGLang (recommended), Transformers HF pipeline, Docker Model Runner
serving_frameworks.notes: HF model card provides ready-to-run commands for vLLM and SGLang. SGLang recommended for production due to MoE/long-context optimizations.

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: When served via vLLM/SGLang with OpenAI-compatible chat completions API, standard tool calling works out of the box with the openai_function shape. MCP protocol support requires an adapter layer (e.g., SGLang MCP bridge). In thinking mode with tool calls, reasoning_content must be passed back in subsequent turns.

models.notes: Preview release (April 2026). Currently the heaviest open-weight MoE at 1.6T total params. Achieves frontier-class coding/math performance (Codeforces 3206 in Think Max mode). Actively used in DeepSeek's own internal agentic workflows (Claude Code, OpenCode). The legacy model names deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner are deprecated and will be removed 2026-07-24; they currently route to deepseek-v4-flash.

Significantly cheaper than V4-Pro at $0.14/$0.28 per 1M in/out. Flash-Max thinking mode achieves near-Pro reasoning with a larger token budget.

max_input_tokens.notes: Max output not separately documented for self-hosted V3.2. When on the hosted API (now deprecated in favor of V4), deepseek-chat was 64K context / 8K output.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Not separately documented for self-hosted deployment.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Not separately documented; deployment-configurable. The legacy hosted API had 8K (non-thinking) / 64K (thinking via deepseek-reasoner) output caps before V4 migration.

extended_context.notes: 163840 is the native max; no separate extended mode.

models.notes: Released 2025-12-01. Predecessor to V4. Still widely self-hosted due to 671B MoE architecture (smaller than V4-Pro's 1.6T). Notable: first DeepSeek model with reasoning integrated into tool-use. Context window is 160K (vs V4's 1M). No longer available as a distinct endpoint on the official hosted API — replaced by V4-Flash. Researchers evaluating lower-resource self-hosting should consider V4-Flash (284B) instead.
